ar-e5efb4d3.stem: Which bone is the keystone of the lateral longitudinal arch of the foot?
ar-e5efb4d3.explanation: The keystone of the medial longitudinal arch is the head of the talus, that of the lateral arch the cuboid. The lateral arch is low and close to the ground.

ar-ca751a1b.stem: What is the most common cause of acquired flatfoot in adults?
ar-ca751a1b.explanation: Tibialis posterior is the most important dynamic support of the medial arch; degeneration and failure of its tendon lead to collapse of the medial arch and valgus of the heel.

ar-a91411e8.stem: A patient who fell onto a plantarflexed foot has midfoot swelling and plantar ecchymosis; the radiograph shows a gap between the bases of the 1st and 2nd metatarsals. What is the most likely diagnosis?
ar-a91411e8.explanation: Plantar ecchymosis and a gap between the 1st and 2nd metatarsal bases are typical signs of a Lisfranc ligament injury; about one in five is missed at first presentation, so it needs careful assessment.

ar-fe1c13ee.stem: Which type of dens fracture has the highest risk of non-union?
options: Type III (extending into the body of the axis)
ar-fe1c13ee.explanation: In the Anderson–D'Alonzo classification a type II fracture crosses the base of the dens; non-union is frequent in this poorly vascularised region. Type III extends into the body of the axis and usually heals.

ar-55929b2d.stem: Where does the sensory innervation of the facet (zygapophyseal) joints come from?
options: Anterior rami of the spinal nerves
Medial branches of the posterior rami of the spinal nerves
Lateral branches of the posterior rami
ar-55929b2d.explanation: Each facet joint is supplied by the medial branches of the posterior rami of two adjacent levels. In facet pain these branches are targeted with blocks or radiofrequency ablation.

ar-dd990884.stem: The sphenomandibular ligament is a remnant of which pharyngeal arch structure?
options: Cartilage of the 1st pharyngeal arch (Meckel's cartilage)
ar-dd990884.explanation: Meckel's cartilage gives rise to the malleus, incus and sphenomandibular ligament. Reichert's cartilage (2nd arch) forms the stapes, styloid process and stylohyoid ligament.

ar-bead98f0.stem: Which forearm ligament has fibres running in the opposite direction to those of the interosseous membrane?
ar-bead98f0.explanation: Fibres of the interosseous membrane run downwards and medially from radius to ulna, whereas the oblique cord descends laterally from the ulnar tuberosity to the radius. It supports the proximal radio-ulnar joint.

ar-5ba07cbd.stem: What is the ligament-poor area on the palmar side of the capitate, through which perilunate dislocations occur, called?
ar-5ba07cbd.explanation: The space of Poirier is the weak area between the radioscaphocapitate and radiolunate ligaments; in perilunate dislocation the capitate separates from the lunate here.

ar-31d4bdc3.stem: Tears in which part of the TFCC do not heal because it is avascular, and require debridement?
ar-31d4bdc3.explanation: Only the outer margin of the TFCC is well vascularised. Central tears do not heal and are treated by arthroscopic debridement, whereas peripheral tears are repaired.

ar-c3fb2f81.stem: Which condition, seen in people whose ulna is longer than the radius (ulnar positive variance), causes wear of the TFCC and lunate?
ar-c3fb2f81.explanation: In ulnar positive variance the ulnar head presses on the TFCC and lunate, causing ulnar-sided pain and cartilage damage of the lunate. Kienböck disease is associated rather with ulnar negative variance.

ar-e6d0e58d.stem: Which is the most important stabilising ligament of the thumb carpometacarpal joint?
ar-e6d0e58d.explanation: The anterior oblique ligament runs from the tubercle of the trapezium to the anteromedial base of the 1st metacarpal; it is also the ligament that holds the small medial fragment in place in a Bennett fracture.

ar-17c5390c.stem: In a Stener lesion, which structure becomes interposed between the torn ulnar collateral ligament and its attachment?
ar-17c5390c.explanation: When the ulnar collateral ligament of the thumb MCP joint ruptures, its end may come to lie on top of the adductor aponeurosis; the interposed aponeurosis prevents healing, so surgery is needed.

ar-dbeaf9b7.stem: Which structure dislocates in a Monteggia fracture?
options: Head of the radius (proximal radio-ulnar joint)
ar-dbeaf9b7.explanation: In a Monteggia fracture a fracture of the proximal third of the ulna is accompanied by dislocation of the radial head. In a Galeazzi fracture a radial shaft fracture is accompanied by dislocation of the distal radio-ulnar joint.

ar-9db62430.stem: Why is posterior dislocation of the sternoclavicular joint an emergency?
options: The medial end of the clavicle can compress the great vessels and trachea behind it.
It also dislocates the shoulder joint.
ar-9db62430.explanation: In posterior dislocation the medial end of the clavicle can compress the brachiocephalic vessels, trachea and oesophagus; unlike anterior dislocation, it may therefore need urgent reduction.

ar-684028b7.stem: How much of the posterior surface of the femoral neck does the hip joint capsule enclose?
options: All of it up to the greater trochanter
ar-684028b7.explanation: Anteriorly the capsule reaches the intertrochanteric line and encloses the whole neck; posteriorly it covers only the medial 2/3 of the neck. Femoral neck fractures are therefore largely intracapsular.

ar-afbcdf8f.stem: Which ligament limits excessive internal rotation of the hip joint?
options: Ligament of the head of the femur
ar-afbcdf8f.explanation: The ischiofemoral ligament spirals from the ischium onto the posterior capsule; it is taut in internal rotation and extension.

ar-eb063057.stem: Which is the most important static stabiliser of the posterolateral corner of the knee?
ar-eb063057.explanation: The posterolateral corner consists of the lateral collateral ligament, popliteus tendon, popliteofibular ligament and capsule; the popliteofibular ligament is the main static restraint to external rotation.

ar-8f7a2217.stem: In the dial test, increased external rotation at both 30° and 90° of knee flexion suggests what?
options: An isolated medial collateral ligament tear
Combined injury of the posterolateral corner and posterior cruciate ligament
An isolated anterior cruciate ligament tear
ar-8f7a2217.explanation: Increased external rotation only at 30° suggests an isolated posterolateral corner injury; at both 30° and 90°, a combined injury of the posterolateral corner and PCL.

ar-cf2d6b19.stem: Which lateral ankle ligament contributes to both the talocrural and subtalar joints?
ar-cf2d6b19.explanation: The calcaneofibular ligament runs from the lateral malleolus to the calcaneus and thus crosses both joints; it is assessed with the talar tilt test.

ar-f8a72f31.stem: Which is the most important structure preventing lateral shift of the talus within the ankle mortise?
options: Deep (tibiotalar) part of the deltoid ligament
Tibionavicular part of the deltoid ligament
ar-f8a72f31.explanation: The deep tibiotalar fibres of the deltoid ligament bind the talus to the medial malleolus; if they tear, the talus shifts laterally, the joint contact area decreases and osteoarthritis develops.

ar-90e61aae.stem: From the calcaneus, to which bones do the two limbs of the bifurcate ligament run?
ar-90e61aae.explanation: The calcaneonavicular and calcaneocuboid limbs of the Y-shaped bifurcate ligament lie on the dorsum of Chopart's joint; its sprain causes pain in front of the sinus tarsi.

ar-c4078aba.stem: What is the typical sign of talocalcaneal coalition on a lateral ankle radiograph?
ar-c4078aba.explanation: In talocalcaneal coalition a continuous C-shaped contour forms between the dome of the talus and the sustentaculum tali. In calcaneonavicular coalition the oblique view shows the 'anteater nose'.

ar-358bf10c.stem: A skier who twisted the knee into external rotation reports sudden pain and instability; after ACL reconstruction, external rotation instability of the knee persists. Which injury may have been missed?
options: Posterolateral corner injury of the knee
ar-358bf10c.explanation: Posterolateral corner injuries often accompany cruciate ligament injuries; if they are not recognised and repaired, the cruciate graft is overloaded and the reconstruction fails.
